reason: The expert search strategy decision explicitly recommends reducing the fuel_penalty scale from -0.1 to -0.05 while keeping all other components identical to iter_001. This is a minimal, targeted change that directly addresses the scale imbalance (fuel_penalty dominance ratio 4.22) without introducing any of the failed patterns from iter_002 through iter_005. The edit scope is small because only one component scale is changed.
preserved_design: success_bonus: scale 100, conditions unchanged (both legs contact, |angle|<0.1, |x|<0.1, y<0.2, |vx|<0.1, |vy|<0.1)
shaping_reward: progress-delta for distance and vertical speed, scale 1.0
orientation_penalty: scale -0.1, applied per step for |angle| + |angular_velocity|
leg_contact_bonus: one-shot event-gated bonus of 10 when both legs first contact
vertical_speed_penalty: scale -1.0, applied when y<0.2 and |vy|>0.5
changed_design: fuel_penalty: scale reduced from -0.1 to -0.05 per unit m_power

target_behavior_plan: The revised reward reduces the fuel_penalty scale from -0.1 to -0.05, halving the dominant penalty. This directly addresses the scale imbalance: the fuel_penalty was 4.22x the next component and 65x the positive objective budget. With the reduced fuel penalty, longer episodes that use main engine for controlled descent will be less costly, allowing the policy to explore landing more aggressively. The success_bonus (100) remains unchanged and provides a strong terminal signal. The shaping_reward (progress-delta) continues to provide positive feedback for reducing distance and vertical speed. The leg_contact_bonus (10) remains one-shot. The crash_penalty (-50) remains unchanged. The orientation_penalty (-0.1) remains unchanged. The vertical_speed_penalty (-1.0) remains unchanged. The expected outcome is that the policy will use main engine more freely near ground, increasing the success_like_terminal_rate from 0.2 to >=0.5 and decreasing timeout_rate from 0.8 to <=0.4.
action_coverage_plan: Action coverage is already 100%. No changes needed. The revised reward should maintain or increase main engine usage for controlled descent and landing.
phase_guidance_plan: Phase 1 (high altitude): shaping_reward encourages descending toward pad, fuel_penalty (now halved) discourages excessive main engine use less strongly. Phase 2 (low altitude): shaping_reward continues, fuel_penalty continues at reduced rate, vertical_speed_penalty discourages hard landings. Phase 3 (touchdown): leg_contact_bonus and success_bonus reward proper landing. The reduced fuel penalty makes all phases less costly, encouraging the policy to explore landing rather than hovering.
payment_mode_plan: success_bonus is sparse (one-shot at terminal success). leg_contact_bonus is event-gated (one-shot). shaping_reward is progress-delta (not repeatable in the same sense). fuel_penalty is dense per-step penalty but now halved. orientation_penalty is dense per-step penalty. vertical_speed_penalty is dense but conditional. crash_penalty is sparse at termination. All positive terms are either sparse, event-gated, or progress-delta. No repeatable positive terms without success.
